title: Only 7% Pass This Nursing Entrance Exam
summary: Connect body systems, observations, numbers and thoughtful care through practical questions.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
Test your understanding of body systems, observations, infection prevention, communication and practical reasoning. Each set brings a different part of nursing-related knowledge into focus.

Choose the best answer from the information shown. Your checkpoints reflect the topic just completed; your final result brings the whole attempt together with an optional review.

Questions avoid country-specific clinical pathways, medication doses and professional-role rules. This entertainment quiz is not an accredited nursing entrance exam, qualification or source of clinical instructions.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited nursing entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Healthcare procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local policy and qualified clinical guidance.

nursing-s1q1.question: Which gas does blood pick up in the lungs?

nursing-s1q2.question: Which organs remove wastes from blood and help regulate water balance?

nursing-s1q3.question: Which system carries rapid signals between the brain and the body?

nursing-s1q4.question: Where are most digested nutrients absorbed?

nursing-s1q5.question: Which blood cells carry most of the oxygen in blood?

nursing-s1q6.question: Which major muscle helps draw air into the lungs?

nursing-s1q7.question: Which heart chamber receives blood returning from the lungs?

nursing-s2q1.question: A pulse changes from 72 to 88 beats per minute. What does the record show?

answers.a1: An increase of 16 beats per minute
answers.a3: An increase of 8 beats per minute
answers.a4: A decrease of 16 beats per minute

nursing-s2q2.question: Earlier, a person spoke comfortably. Now they pause between short phrases to breathe. What changed?

answers.a3: The record proves a specific diagnosis

nursing-s2q3.question: Which observation describes a new change in alertness?

answers.a2: The room lights were switched on
answers.a4: The chart has a new page

nursing-s2q4.question: Which description records a breathing rate?

nursing-s2q5.question: What does a pulse oximeter estimate?

nursing-s2q6.question: Why should a reassuring device reading not replace assessment of new symptoms?

answers.a1: One number proves all body systems are healthy
answers.a3: Every device always gives random values
answers.a4: Measurements have limitations and need context

nursing-s2q7.question: Which change calls for prompt qualified assessment?

answers.a1: A different pen used for notes
answers.a2: New breathing difficulty with reduced alertness

nursing-s3q1.question: Hands are visibly dirty. Which cleaning method is appropriate?

answers.a2: Put gloves on over the dirt

nursing-s3q2.question: What should happen after protective gloves are removed?

answers.a1: Clean hands only if a glove tore
answers.a2: Keep the gloves for another person

nursing-s3q3.question: Which container is designed for used needles and other sharps?

answers.a1: An open tray for later sorting

nursing-s3q4.question: A task may splash body fluid toward the face. Which protection addresses that risk?

nursing-s3q5.question: Shared observation equipment has been used. What should happen before reuse?

answers.a1: Cover old marks with a label
answers.a3: Clean it using the approved method
answers.a4: Use it unchanged if it looks shiny

nursing-s3q6.question: A sterile package is torn before use. What is the safe conclusion?

answers.a1: The printed date cancels the tear
answers.a2: The contents are sterile if they look clean

nursing-s3q7.question: Which statement about protective gloves is correct?

answers.a1: The same pair is suitable for every patient
answers.a2: They stay clean regardless of what they touch
answers.a3: They do not replace hand hygiene

nursing-s4q1.question: A person says, “I’m worried about what happens next.” What is the best opening?

answers.a2: Acknowledge the worry and invite questions
answers.a3: Promise there is no possible risk

nursing-s4q2.question: Someone wants to discuss a sensitive concern in a busy public area. What protects privacy?

answers.a1: Write the details on a public board

nursing-s4q3.question: A person has not understood an explanation. What helps check understanding?

answers.a1: Ask another patient to answer for them
answers.a3: Treat a nod as proof of understanding
answers.a4: Explain plainly and ask them to describe it in their own words

nursing-s4q4.question: Before a non-urgent examination, what should the person receive?

answers.a1: A decision made by the nearest visitor
answers.a2: Only a form with no explanation
answers.a3: An assurance that questions are not allowed
answers.a4: A clear explanation and an opportunity to consent

nursing-s4q5.question: A person declines having students present. What is the respectful response?

answers.a1: Assume silence later cancels the choice
answers.a4: Respect the choice and protect privacy

nursing-s4q6.question: A language barrier makes an important discussion difficult. What is the best support?

answers.a3: Asking a young child to interpret sensitive details

nursing-s4q7.question: A person with hearing difficulty asks you to repeat yourself. What is helpful?

answers.a2: Face them and check their preferred way to communicate

nursing-s5q1.question: A record shows 700 mL plus 250 mL. What is the total?

nursing-s5q2.question: How many millilitres are in 1.5 L?

nursing-s5q3.question: How much time passes from 09:20 to 10:05?

nursing-s5q4.question: You count 9 breaths in 30 seconds. What is the equivalent rate per minute?

nursing-s5q5.question: A recorded total rises from 600 mL to 900 mL. What is the percentage increase?

nursing-s5q6.question: Divide 1.2 L equally across four recorded periods. How much belongs to each?

nursing-s5q7.question: Three sealed boxes hold eight items each. How many items are there?

nursing-s6q1.question: A note says “left arm” but the handover says “right arm”. What needs clarification?

nursing-s6q2.question: A measurement is written as “12” with no unit. What is missing?

answers.a2: The unit needed to interpret the value

nursing-s6q3.question: Which record clearly separates a reported symptom from an observation?

answers.a2: “Definitely has a diagnosis I have not assessed”
answers.a3: “Nothing happened because the chart is blank”

nursing-s6q4.question: Why include the time beside a new observation?

answers.a2: To prove the cause by itself
answers.a4: To place it in the sequence of events

nursing-s6q5.question: A chart has no entry for a scheduled measurement. What can you conclude?

nursing-s6q6.question: Which entry records what happened most clearly?

nursing-s6q7.question: Why compare current observations with earlier ones?

answers.a3: To avoid looking at the person
answers.a4: To prove a diagnosis from any difference

nursing-s7q1.question: A person reports pain but looks calm. What is appropriate?

answers.a1: Take their report seriously and assess it
answers.a3: Wait until they cry before listening
answers.a4: Assume calm appearance proves there is no pain

nursing-s7q2.question: A person needs help moving and feels unsteady. What comes first?

answers.a1: Assume every person needs the same method
answers.a2: Assess the help and equipment needed before moving
answers.a3: Pull them quickly by one arm
answers.a4: Ask them to rush before becoming tired

nursing-s7q3.question: What helps someone take part in a decision about their care?

answers.a2: A decision based only on room availability
answers.a3: A promise that no questions are needed

nursing-s7q4.question: A person asks for more privacy during routine care. What is appropriate?

answers.a1: Discuss the concern across the room
answers.a2: Ignore the request because the task is routine
answers.a3: Provide appropriate privacy while maintaining safety

nursing-s7q5.question: Which question avoids assuming how someone feels?

nursing-s7q6.question: A person’s preferred name differs from the name used by staff. What is helpful?

answers.a1: Ask how they prefer to be addressed

nursing-s7q7.question: What is the purpose of involving a person in their care plan?

answers.a2: To understand their needs, preferences and goals
answers.a4: To make them responsible for every clinical decision

nursing-s8q1.question: Which handover opening gives a useful time and change?

answers.a4: “At 14:20, breathing became faster and alertness decreased”

nursing-s8q2.question: You are unsure whether a reported allergy is documented correctly. What should you communicate?

answers.a1: Only the colour of the record
answers.a2: A guess stated as a confirmed fact
answers.a3: The uncertainty and the need to verify it
answers.a4: That it cannot matter if the chart is unclear

nursing-s8q3.question: An urgent request was spoken in a noisy room. What helps confirm it was understood?

answers.a1: Ask the recipient to repeat the key information
answers.a2: Repeat it only to an unrelated visitor
answers.a4: Assume hearing the first word was enough

nursing-s8q4.question: Which information should come first when handing over a sudden deterioration?

answers.a2: The order of routine stationery supplies
answers.a3: The person’s meal choice last week
answers.a4: The new concern and current observations

nursing-s8q5.question: A colleague asks what you actually observed. Which answer is most precise?

answers.a1: “They were definitely developing a disease I have not assessed”
answers.a2: “They became drowsy at 11:10 and were harder to engage”

nursing-s8q6.question: A task is handed over between staff. What makes responsibility clearer?

answers.a1: Agree who will do what and when
answers.a2: Give different instructions to each person

nursing-s8q7.question: A written note conflicts with the person’s current account. What is the careful response?

answers.a3: Clarify the difference and document accurately

nursing-s9q1.question: Person A is comfortable after walking. Person B is newly confused and struggling to breathe. Who needs urgent attention?

answers.a1: Neither until a diagnosis is known

nursing-s9q2.question: A single reading differs from earlier values but seems inconsistent with the person’s condition. What is appropriate?

answers.a1: Assume all earlier values must be false
answers.a2: Check the measurement and assess the person
answers.a3: Treat it as a complete diagnosis

nursing-s9q3.question: Which statement distinguishes a symptom from a diagnosis?

answers.a1: Dizziness describes an experience but does not identify its cause
answers.a2: A diagnosis is just the time written on a chart
answers.a3: Every report of dizziness proves the same disease
answers.a4: A symptom can never be reported by the person

answers.a2: Their combined pattern can be more informative
answers.a3: Only the largest number ever matters
answers.a4: One normal value cancels every abnormal sign

nursing-s9q5.question: A new severe concern appears while routine paperwork is unfinished. What should guide the priority?

answers.a1: The shortest task on the list
answers.a2: Finishing the paperwork regardless of condition
answers.a3: The person’s immediate needs and appropriate escalation
answers.a4: The time until the next break

nursing-s9q6.question: A proposed action is outside your training. What is the appropriate response?

answers.a2: Seek qualified help and follow the relevant guidance
answers.a3: Ask an untrained visitor to carry it out
answers.a4: Proceed because the equipment is nearby

nursing-s9q7.question: Which phrase expresses a reasonable limit of the available evidence?

answers.a1: “No diagnosis means there is no concern”
answers.a2: “This change needs assessment; the cause is not yet established”
answers.a3: “An earlier normal value rules out later illness”

nursing-s10q1.question: An airway blockage prevents air reaching the lungs. What follows most directly?

answers.a1: Less oxygen can enter the blood
answers.a4: The kidneys replace lung gas exchange

nursing-s10q2.question: A person drinks 0.75 L, then 425 mL. What total is recorded?

nursing-s10q3.question: Earlier: alert and breathing comfortably. Now: pale, confused and breathing faster. What does this suggest?

answers.a2: No concern unless all values are missing
answers.a3: A specific diagnosis proven without assessment

nursing-s10q4.question: You need to discuss private information and check understanding. Which approach meets both needs?

answers.a1: Use a private setting, plain language and a check-back
answers.a2: Discuss it loudly and ask only for a nod
answers.a3: Use jargon in the public waiting area
answers.a4: Give no explanation to protect privacy

nursing-s10q5.question: A clean task follows contact with body fluid. What should happen before continuing?

answers.a1: Use appropriate hand hygiene and clean protective equipment
answers.a2: Wipe gloves on the bed cover
answers.a4: Assume the next patient has the same risk

nursing-s10q6.question: A record rises from 1,000 mL to 1,250 mL. What is the increase?

nursing-s10q7.question: A person reports worsening symptoms despite an earlier normal check. What is the safest approach?

answers.a1: Dismiss it because the earlier check was normal
answers.a2: Reassess the current concern and seek appropriate help
answers.a4: Treat the earlier check as a permanent guarantee
